title: Convexity, simple connectivity, and the hole obstruction
section: Green’s Theorem ▷ Path Independence and Gradient Fields
terms: convex region; simply connected region; curl-free planar field; closed-path criterion; hole obstruction.

exposition.text:
A set is convex if it contains the line segment joining every pair of its points. An open con-
nected region is simply connected if every loop can be continuously contracted to a point within
it. For planar domains this expresses the absence of holes. Convex domains are simply con-
nected, but the converse fails.

but integrates to 2π around the positively oriented unit circle. Path independence, existence
of a potential, and vanishing of all closed-path integrals remain equivalent on open connected
domains; simple connectivity is a sufficient global hypothesis for the derivative test, not a hy-
pothesis required for those three equivalences themselves.

question.text:

A C vector field (M, N) on the annulus 1 < x + y < 4 satisfies M = N . Which additional
y x
condition guarantees a potential on this annulus?
(A) It is bounded
(B) Its integral around every closed piecewise smooth path is zero
(C) It has no zero vector values
(D) Its integral along one radial segment is zero
(E) It is tangent to both boundary circles

solution.text:
Vanishing of every closed-path integral makes integrals between endpoints independent
of path. Integrating from a fixed base point then defines a potential. The annulus is not
simply connected, so equality of cross-partials alone is insufficient.

What is the counterclockwise integral of (−y dx + x dy)/(x + y ) around (x − 3) + y = 1?
(A) It is undefined (B) 0 (C) π (D) 2π (E) −2π

solution.text:
The disk enclosed by this circle avoids the origin. The field is smooth there and has zero
scalar curl, so Green’s theorem gives zero integral.

question.text:
2 2 2
Let D = R \ {(x, 0) : x ≤ 0}. Which statement about D and F = (−y, x)/(x + y ) on D is
correct?
(A) D is convex and F has no potential.
(B) D is not convex but is simply connected, and F has a potential.
(C) D is not simply connected and F has no potential.
(D) D is convex and every potential must be constant.
(E) F fails the equal-cross-partial condition on D.

solution.text:
The segment joining (−1, 1) to (−1, −1) crosses the removed ray, so D is not convex. How-
ever polar coordinates with r > 0 and −π < θ < π identify it continuously with a strip (use
log r), so every loop contracts. The single-valued angle θ = Arg(x + iy) on this slit plane has
gradient F and is a potential.

question.text:
A continuously differentiable curl-free planar field is defined on a convex open set. Which must
hold?
(A) Its divergence vanishes
(B) Its potential is unique without a constant
(C) Its integral around every closed piecewise smooth curve is zero
(D) The field is identically zero
(E) The domain is bounded

solution.text:
A convex open set is simply connected, so the curl-free field has a potential. The fundamen-
tal theorem for line integrals then makes every closed-curve integral zero.
